Huawei Lagrange Mathematics and Computing Research Center · Paris (city center)

:loudspeaker: Immediate Internship Opening (Fall / Winter / Spring): While we have received a large number of candidatures for Summer, we still have open spots for internships starting now and ending around March–April. This is ideal for PhD students, gap-year students, or candidates with flexible availability outside the standard summer cycle. If you are available to start now, please mention your availability in your email!

We research the intersection of artificial intelligence and formal mathematics, spanning autoformalization, automated reasoning, and theorem proving. Our work ranges from translating informal mathematics (olympiad problems, textbooks, research statements) into faithful formal statements in proof assistants like Lean 4, to automated proof generation, tactic prediction, and formal proof verification. A central challenge is semantic fidelity and logical rigor: ensuring formal statements truly match intended meanings and generating valid, verified proofs. Our research develops agentic pipelines, multi-dimensional semantic evaluation, and iterative self-correction loops that go beyond simple type-checking and line-by-line compilation.

To see our recent work and approach in action, check out our paper: arxiv#2609.35790

We collaborate closely with Huawei’s Pangu LLM and OpenJiuwen (agent harness) to push formalization, automated theorem proving, evaluation, and tooling that advance both AI for mathematics and mathematical practice itself.

Tracks & Qualifications

The project sits at the intersection of three tracks. We welcome strong candidates in any one of them:

  1. Mathematical Theory & Logic — Proof theory, type theory, foundations, formal logic
  2. Formalization & Interactive Theorem Proving — Lean 4 (or Rocq / Isabelle)
  3. Engineering & ML Systems — LLM inference, agent frameworks, pipelines, reasoning systems

Location: On-site at the Lagrange Center in central Paris

Duration: 6 months preferred (3 months minimum)

Requirements

Must Have:

Excellence in at least one track:

  • Theory / Logic: Proof theory, type theory, or formal mathematics; OR
  • Formalization & Proving: Strong Lean 4 (or Rocq / Isabelle); OR
  • LLM / ML Infra: Inference stacks (e.g., vLLM, liteLLM), agentic systems, pipeline engineering

Core Technical & AI Tooling Skills:

  • Python Proficiency: Strong practical coding ability in Python across all tracks
  • AI-Assisted Development: Proficiency with AI development tools, coding assistants, and agentic IDE frameworks (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, ...) to accelerate development and research workflows

Competition Background: Proven track record in official competitive math, informatics, or problem-solving competitions. Target backgrounds include:

  • Olympiads: IMO, IOI, IPhO, IChO
  • Programming & Systems: ICPC, CTF, Supercomputing (ASC), EUCYS
  • AI & Data Science: Kaggle (Top ranks / Masters / Grandmasters)
  • Math Modeling & Open Challenges: IMC, MCM/ICM, or Huawei Tech Arena

Preferred:

  • Mathematics students or candidates with strong theoretical backgrounds
  • Solid applied mathematics background if not pure theory
  • Strong GitHub / portfolio demonstrating clear ownership and practical tool usage (not just vibe-coded projects)

How to Apply

If you are interested, please send an email to thomas.hirtz@huawei.com with the subject line:

Internship - AI4Math - [Your Name]

Please include the following in your email:

  1. Your Resume / CV
  2. A list of official competitions participated in (including year, stage/tier, and awards/results)
  3. Link to your portfolio, GitHub, or personal website

  4. A short Motivation Statement: Feel free to keep this concise—you do not need to write a formal cover letter or answer every point. As a guide, consider covering:

    • Project Motivation: What draws you to this project specifically?
    • Technical Perspective: What is your view or experience regarding AI-assisted formalization tools? (Feel free to share your high-level perspective if you are new to them.)
    • Background & Fit: What aspect of your background makes this project a good fit for you—even if your experience isn't a 1-to-1 match?
    • (Optional) Any additional context or details you would like us to know.

Note on Eligibility: Please note that due to strict internal guidelines, we are strictly only permitted to consider candidates who possess a documented competition track record (e.g., IMO, IOI, ICPC, Kaggle, IMC, etc.). Candidates without a competitive background unfortunately cannot be processed for this role.
